# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# Expectation for the doctor check `units_present` (DESIGN.md §7.1) against input/.
# How to read this file: tests/fixtures/doctor/node_layout/expect.json. The _env caveat is the same one
# tests/fixtures/doctor/unit_no_password_in_argv/expect.json records at length: §2i freezes
# FMONERO_PROC_ROOT and FMONERO_SYSTEMCTL_FIXTURE and NEITHER points the doctor at a directory of unit
# FILES, which this check and five others need. Phase 0 records that gap rather than filling it.
#
# A `pass` FIXTURE FOR THIS CHECK CANNOT BE WRITTEN, AND SAYING SO IS PART OF THE FIXTURE.
# §7.1's condition is that both unit files exist AND MATCH units::render_* BYTE FOR BYTE. Those bytes
# embed the machine: $HOME (the wallet unit's absolute --wallet-dir, deliberately not %h so that
# wallet_dir_matches_unit can compare it literally -- §4.2), settings.wallet.port, and the network
# segment from settings.node.network. A committed file can match them only on the machine and settings
# that produced it. The correct test for the passing case is therefore NOT a fixture but a round trip:
# render, write, re-read, compare -- which the Phase 2 doctor agent's class-B round-trip gate already
# does under FMONERO_STATE_DIR.
# SO THIS FIXTURE IS THE FAILING CASE, and it is the one a round trip cannot produce.
#
# THIS CASE: BOTH UNITS EXIST BUT HAVE DRIFTED. Each file's own header names its changes:
#   node unit    Restart=always instead of on-failure (so `node down` would be undone by systemd),
#                plus a Wants=fmonero-wallet-rpc.service that §4.2 forbids on a monerod unit
#   wallet unit  StateDirectoryMode=0700 REMOVED -- systemd then defaults the directory to 0755, and it
#                holds the wallet daemon's credential and its log (§2c, §4.2, §2b.7)
# NEITHER DRIFT IS A FLAG A GREP WOULD FIND, which is the point of having a byte comparison at all:
# unit_loopback, unit_no_password_in_argv, unit_no_node_wants, wallet_dir_matches_unit and
# wallet_port_consistent each look for one specific thing, and units_present is what notices everything
# else -- including a hand-edit nobody anticipated.
# status `warn` and severity `warn`, from §7.1's own row. It is NOT an error: a drifted unit still runs,
# and §7.1's fix is to rewrite it.
# `fixable` TRUE, class B, and the Action is fixed by §7.1: WriteFile{unit path, units::render_*(ctx),
# 0o644} FOLLOWED BY RunArgv{["systemctl","--user","daemon-reload"], inverse: the same}. A unit
# rewritten without a reload is a fixer that reports success and changes nothing.
# THE PROVENANCE HEADERS IN input/*.service ARE THEMSELVES DRIFT, so this case would report `warn` even
# with every other line correct. That is honest rather than convenient: a fixture whose only defect is
# its own header would be a fixture that tests the header.
